problem: "Secondary servers at stratum 2 and below take time from a higher level" is ambiguous: a stratum 2 server actually takes time from a server with a lower stratum number, and a student may read "higher level" as a higher stratum number.
fix: Write: "A secondary server at stratum 2 (and below) takes time from a server with a smaller stratum number, that is, one step closer to the reference clock."

problem: "Treating Cristian's correction as exact; it is exact only when the two one-way delays are equal" contradicts the first bullet, which also requires the server's processing time to be zero. With equal one-way delays d and server processing time p, the estimate is off by p/2.
fix: Write: "Treating Cristian's correction as exact. It is exact only when the two one-way delays are equal and the server replies immediately, so its processing time is negligible; otherwise the error can be up to RTT/2."

problem: "Where no such bound is acceptable, use logical clocks" suggests logical clocks are a stronger substitute for real time. Logical clocks give only causal ordering and carry no real-time value, so a student may think they solve the accuracy problem.
fix: Write: "When an application needs only the order of events and not real time, logical clocks are enough (Chapter 4.6); they cannot give a real-time bound."

problem: The definition matches the distributed-systems textbooks, but tools such as ntpd and chrony print "offset" for the time difference and "skew" (or frequency) for the rate difference, so a student reading tool output will be confused.
fix: Add one line: "Careful: NTP tools print the time difference as offset and the rate difference as skew or frequency, which is the opposite naming from the distributed-systems use above."
